sunday.themeNote: This week's readings share one quiet truth: God often shows up not in the loud or dramatic moments, but in the gentle and unexpected ones. Elijah finds God in a whisper. Peter finds Jesus reaching for him in the middle of a storm. Together, these stories invite us to slow down and notice where God might already be close.

readings.label: First Reading
readings.fullText:
At the mountain of God, Horeb,
Elijah came to a cave where he took shelter.
Then the LORD said to him,
“Go outside and stand on the mountain before the LORD;
the LORD will be passing by.”
A strong and heavy wind was rending the mountains
and crushing rocks before the LORD—
but the LORD was not in the wind.
After the wind there was an earthquake—
but the LORD was not in the earthquake.
After the earthquake there was fire—
but the LORD was not in the fire.
After the fire there was a tiny whispering sound.
When he heard this,
Elijah hid his face in his cloak
and went and stood at the entrance of the cave.
readings.summary: The prophet Elijah is hiding in a cave, worn out and afraid. God tells him to step outside, and a powerful wind tears through the mountains, then an earthquake shakes the ground, then fire blazes past. But God is not in any of those. After all the noise and force, there is a tiny, quiet sound, and that is where Elijah meets God.

reflection.reflection: God passed by not in the earthquake or the fire, but in a sound so small Elijah almost missed it. This passage invites us to consider that God might be closer than the noise around us suggests.
reflection.question: When during your week do you have even a few quiet minutes, and what do you usually fill them with?

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.fullText:
R. (8) Lord, let us see your kindness, and grant us your salvation.
I will hear what God proclaims;
the LORD — for he proclaims peace.
Near indeed is his salvation to those who fear him,
glory dwelling in our land.
R. Lord, let us see your kindness, and grant us your salvation.
Kindness and truth shall meet;
justice and peace shall kiss.
Truth shall spring out of the earth,
and justice shall look down from heaven.
R. Lord, let us see your kindness, and grant us your salvation.
The LORD himself will give his benefits;
our land shall yield its increase.
Justice shall walk before him,
and prepare the way of his steps.
R. Lord, let us see your kindness, and grant us your salvation.
readings.summary: This psalm is a prayer asking God to show his love and bring his peace. It paints a picture of a world where kindness and truth go hand in hand, and where justice and peace belong together. The people are trusting that God will keep his promises and make things right.

reflection.reflection: The psalm trusts that kindness and peace are not just wishes but things that can take root in real life. It is an invitation to expect goodness, even when things feel uncertain.
reflection.question: Is there a situation in your life right now where you are waiting to see if things will get better?

readings.label: Second Reading
readings.summary: Paul is writing to Christians in Rome, and he is heartbroken. He loves his own Jewish people deeply and is in real pain because he wants them to know Jesus too. He lists all the gifts God gave them throughout history, including the fact that Jesus himself came from their people.

reflection.reflection: Paul's love for his people is so strong it almost breaks him. This passage shows that deep care for others, even when it hurts, is something God sees and honors.
reflection.question: Is there someone in your life you worry about, someone you wish things were different for?

readings.label: Gospel
readings.fullText:
After he had fed the people, Jesus made the disciples get into a boat
and precede him to the other side,
while he dismissed the crowds.
After doing so, he went up on the mountain by himself to pray.
When it was evening he was there alone.
Meanwhile the boat, already a few miles offshore,
was being tossed about by the waves, for the wind was against it.
During the fourth watch of the night,
he came toward them walking on the sea.
When the disciples saw him walking on the sea they were terrified.
“It is a ghost,” they said, and they cried out in fear.
At once Jesus spoke to them, “Take courage, it is I; do not be afraid.”
Peter said to him in reply,
“Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the water.”
He said, “Come.”
Peter got out of the boat and began to walk on the water toward Jesus.
But when he saw how strong the wind was he became frightened;
and, beginning to sink, he cried out, “Lord, save me!”
Immediately Jesus stretched out his hand and caught Peter,
and said to him, “O you of little faith, why did you doubt?”
After they got into the boat, the wind died down.
Those who were in the boat did him homage, saying,
“Truly, you are the Son of God.”
readings.summary: Jesus sends his disciples ahead by boat while he stays behind to pray. A storm hits and the boat is getting tossed around in the dark. Jesus walks out to them on the water, and they are terrified. He tells them not to be afraid. Peter asks to walk out to him, and he does, until he looks at the waves and starts to sink. Jesus grabs him right away, and when they both climb into the boat, the storm stops.

reflection.reflection: Peter steps out of the boat and actually walks on water, until fear takes over. Jesus does not lecture him for long. He just reaches out and catches him. That kind of immediate, no-hesitation help is what this story is really about.
reflection.question: Think of a moment when you felt like you were starting to go under in some situation. Did you feel like you had someone to reach out to?
